description: How an older event is read as the current version. A published version is never edited; a reader upcasts on the way in (contract/upcast.py is the reference; TypeScript, Rust, Kotlin and Swift port the same rules and the shared vectors prove them).

upcasters.rule: Version 1 knew one currency: every amount was an integer RWF, and RWF has no minor unit, so a version 1 amount is already an integer in its minor unit. The upcaster sets schema_version to 2 and adds currency "RWF" to every payload that carries money and had no currency field (PaymentRecorded, ReturnRecorded, ProductCreated). SaleRecorded already carried its currency. Nothing else changes: no amount is rescaled, no field is removed, the signature and hash chain of the stored version 1 event stay as they were, because the upcast is applied when the event is read, never written back.

Version 3 adds an optional side to every payload: internal (the workspace, using a service for one's own affairs) or external (the Storefront, offering to others and earning). Every version 2 event was written before Storefronts existed, so the upcaster sets schema_version to 3 and side "internal" when the payload has none. Nothing else changes: no field is removed or renamed, no amount is touched, and the stored version 2 event, its signature and its hash chain stay as they were, because the upcast is applied when the event is read, never written back.
